item_1765032653875.label: Request Cribl.Cloud Org
item_1765032653875.title: Requesting A Cribl.Cloud Organization [CUSTOMER]
item_1765032653875.content:
Register at https://cribl.cloud/signup/ using a work email. Verify the account and create the organization. Select the region and Workspace offered by the current console; confirm residency and product availability before provisioning. Confirm the POV subscription and entitlements with the account team.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/cloud-initial-setup.md

item_1765040147287.label: Invite Cribl SE to Cribl.Cloud Org
item_1765040147287.title: Invite the Cribl Solutions Engineer (SE) to your Cribl.Cloud organization as an Admin [CUSTOMER]
item_1765040147287.content:
Invite the SE through member management. Grant only the organization, Workspace and product permissions required for the agreed POV. Organization Admin access is not a prerequisite for every task and does not itself upgrade a subscription. Confirm invitations and remove temporary access at the end of the POV.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/iam/permissions.md

item_1765147098771.label: Syslog
item_1765147098771.title: Configure Syslog Source in Cribl [CUSTOMER & CRIBL]
item_1765147098771.content:
**No TLS Method:**
- [ ] Create a new Syslog source: **Data > Sources > Syslog > Add Source**
- [ ] Provide a relevant name for your Source: eg. PaloAlto_Syslog
- [ ] Default port for **UDP** or **TCP** is **9514**
- [ ] Click **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**

**TLS method:**
- [ ] Clone existing **in_syslog_tls** source under **Data > Sources > Syslog**
- [ ] Open **in_syslog_tls**, click **Clone Source** at the bottom.
- [ ] Provide a relevant name for your Source: eg. PaloAlto_Syslog_tls
- [ ] Default port is **TCP 6514**
- [ ] Verify TLS Settings:
  - Enabled
  - **Private key path**: $CRIBL_CLOUD_KEY
  - **Certificate path**: $CRIBL_CLOUD_CRT
  - **Minimum TLS version**: TLSv1.2
- [ ] Click **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**

For more details, refer to [Syslog Source Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/edge/sources-syslog/).

item_1765147334070.label: Google Pub/Sub
item_1765147334070.title: Configure Google Pub/Sub Source in Cribl [CUSTOMER & CRIBL]
item_1765147334070.content:
- [ ] In Cribl Stream, go to **Data > Sources > Google Pub/Sub**, then click **Add Source** button.
- [ ] Provide a relevant name for the Source. eg. Google_PubSub_[TOPICNAME]
- [ ] Provide the Topic ID and Subscription ID from the Pub/Sub topic.
- [ ] Click **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**

For more details, refer to [Google Cloud Pub/Sub Source Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-google_pubsub/).

item_1765147528042.label: GCP Audit Logs (Vendor Side Config)
item_1765147528042.title: Configure GCP Audit Logs [CUSTOMER]
item_1765147528042.content:
Create or identify a Google Cloud Logging sink, Pub/Sub topic and dedicated Cribl subscription. Grant the sink identity publishing access and the Cribl identity subscriber access according to the Source guide. Reuse a topic only with a separate subscription for each independent consumer: sharing a subscription distributes messages between consumers. Configure the actual subscription in Cribl, generate a test audit event and verify delivery and acknowledgements. Confirm vendor-side steps in the current Google Cloud console.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-google_pubsub.md

item_1765316057530.label: Hybrid Worker Node (Linux)
item_1765316057530.title: Deploy Hybrid Worker Node (Linux) [CUSTOMER & CRIBL]
item_1765316057530.content:
Select the hybrid Worker Group and generate its bootstrap command in the current console. Check Linux requirements and sizing before installation. Run the generated command on the target host without copying a token from an example. Allow outbound control-plane connectivity on 4200 and 443 to the documented endpoints. Confirm enrollment, version compatibility and configuration deployment.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/cloud-enterprise.md
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/requirements.md
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/ports.md

item_1765316616468.label: Panorama or Strata (Syslog)
item_1765316616468.title: Configure Panorama or Strata (Syslog) to send to Cribl [CUSTOMER]
item_1765316616468.content:
Configure the Syslog Source first and record its actual endpoint, transport, port and TLS settings. In Panorama/Strata, configure the supported forwarding profile and apply it to the intended log types. If using TLS, trust the current certificate issuer chain presented by that endpoint; do not pin a historical Google certificate chain from an example. Validate name matching, certificate validity and a sample log. Vendor-specific menus and certificate import steps require confirmation against the installed PAN-OS version.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-syslog.md

item_1765423201492.label: Strata (HEC)
item_1765423201492.title: Configure Strata to send logs to Cribl.Cloud via HEC [CUSTOMER]
item_1765423201492.content:
Confirm that the installed Strata product/version supports the required HEC payload. Configure the Cribl HEC Source and copy its real endpoint and token into the supported sender configuration. HEC authorization uses the Splunk token scheme. Do not assume 8088 is externally reachable in a managed Cloud Worker Group; use its documented endpoint and port mapping. Send a test event and verify headers, parsing, routing and delivery. Validate vendor-side HTTP forwarding with the customer.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-splunk-hec.md

item_1765423459750.label: CrowdStrike NG SIEM
item_1765423459750.title: Configure CrowdStrike NG SIEM Connector [CUSTOMER]
item_1765423459750.content:
Prepare the receiving service before configuring the Cribl Destination. Confirm: CrowdStrike connector / ingestion endpoint / parser. Use the authentication, payload and permissions required by the linked guide and current customer subscription. Do not reuse example endpoints or secrets. Configure the Cribl Destination with those values, test connectivity, send a sample event and verify the final record, timestamp and fields in the receiver. Record throughput, retry behavior and any rate limits. Vendor console navigation and licensing must be validated for the installed service.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-crowdstrike-next-gen-siem.md

item_1765423653216.label: CrowdStrike NG SIEM
item_1765423653216.title: Configure CrowdStrike NG SIEM Destination [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765423653216.content:
- [ ] In **Cribl Stream**, navigate to **Data > Destinations**.
- [ ] Select **CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM** and click **Add Destination**.
- [ ] Fill in the required fields:
- **Output ID**: Provide a unique name for the destination.
- **Next-Gen SIEM endpoint**: Enter the **URL** generated in the CrowdStrike platform (API URL).
- **Request format**: Select JSON for standard ingest.
- Under **Authentication**, choose **Manual** and enter the **authentication token (API key)**.

For more details, refer to the [CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM Destination Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-crowdstrike-next-gen-siem/).

item_1765480406274.label: Edge Node (Windows)
item_1765480406274.title: Deploy Edge Node (Windows) [CUSTOMER & CRIBL]
item_1765480406274.content:
Select the Edge Fleet and generate the Windows installation command for the intended Leader and Fleet. Use the current installation guide and matching package/chart version rather than a frozen version or example token. Check service-account permissions and resource allocation. Edge minimums: approximately 1 GHz CPU, 1024 MB RAM and 5 GB free space per operational volume; size for the workload. Confirm enrollment and collection. Local Edge API defaults to 9420; expose it only when needed.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/edge/requirements.md

item_1765484866509.label: Google SecOps - Cloud Chronicle API
item_1765484866509.title: Configure Google Cloud Chronicle API Destination [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765484866509.content:
- [ ] Go to **Data > Destinations**.
- [ ] Select the **Google Cloud Chronicle API** tile.
- [ ] Click **Add Destination** button in the upper right.
- [ ] Fill in the required fields:
- **Output ID**: Provide a unique name for the destination.
- **Default log type**: Select the log type from the drop down that maps to the SecOps parser.
- **GCP project ID**: Find this in Google SecOps in Settings > Profile
- **GCP instance**: The Customer ID under Organization Details in Google SecOps.
- **Region**: Select the region of your Google SecOps instance.
- **Log text field**: set to _raw
- [ ] Select **Authentication > Authentication method**, and choose **Service account credentials**.
- [ ] Paste the service account credentials as **JSON**.
- [ ] **Save**, **Commit & Deploy**

For more details, refer to the [Google Cloud Chronicle API Destination Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-google-chronicle-api/).

item_1765485125039.label: Cribl HTTP
item_1765485125039.title: Configure Cribl_HTTP Destination in Cribl Edge [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765485125039.content:
*This is so Edge can send logs to Cribl Stream. Customers are not double billed for sending the logs to Stream.*

- [ ] Select **Products > Cribl Edge**
- [ ] Under **Fleets**, select the appropriate Fleet.
- [ ] Navigate to **More > Destinations**
- [ ] Select **Cribl HTTP**, click **Add Destination**
- [ ] Configure the Destination
- **Output ID**: Provide a unique name for the Destination
- **Cribl Worker endpoints**: Provide the endpoint of the hybrid Stream Worker Node: Use the format: http://IP_ADDRESS:10200/
- [ ] Click **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**

For more details, refer to the [Cribl HTTP Destination Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-cribl-http/).

item_1765512482002.label: Splunk HEC
item_1765512482002.title: Configure Splunk HEC Source in Cribl [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765512482002.content:
- [ ] Navigate to **Data > Sources** in **Cribl Stream**.
- [ ] Select **Splunk HEC** and click **Add Source**.
- [ ] Fill in the required fields:
- **Input ID**: Provide a unique name for the source.
- **Port**: set the port number if desired. (default is 8088).
- [ ] Select **Auth Tokens** on left panel then click **Add Token** button.
- [ ] Enter token or click **Generate** button to create a new token.
- [ ] Capture the **token** for configuration of your data source.
- [ ] Under **Products > Cribl > Data Sources**, scroll to **in_splunk_hec** and copy the **Ingest Address** for configuration of your data source.
- [ ] **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**.

For more details, refer to [Splunk HEC Source Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-splunk-hec/).

item_1765512671204.label: Cribl_HTTP
item_1765512671204.title: Configure Cribl_HTTP Source in Cribl [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765512671204.content:
- [ ] Click on the default **Cribl_HTTP** source: **Data > Sources > Cribl HTTP**
- [ ] Enable the Source and ensure it is listening on **10200** (default port)
- [ ] Click **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**.

For more details, refer to [Cribl HTTP Source Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-cribl-http/).

item_1765513017350.label: Edge - Windows Event Logs
item_1765513017350.title: Configure Windows Event Logs Source in Cribl Edge [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765513017350.content:
- [ ] Select **Products > Cribl Edge**.
- [ ] Under **Fleets**, select the appropriate Fleet.
- [ ] Navigate to **Routing > Collect**.
- [ ] Select **Add Source** and select **Windows Event Logs**.
- [ ] Configure the Source
- **Input ID**: Provide a unique name for the Source.
- **Event logs**: Enter one or more event logs to collect.  Security is there by default.
  - Click **Add log** to specify more event logs (Application, System, etc..)
- **Optional Settings**:
  - **Read mode**: From last entry – read only new events OR Entire Log (suggest using From last entry for POV).
  - **Event format**: JSON (options are JSON or XML)
  - **Render Event Message Strings**: Toggle this to ON.
- [ ] Click **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**.

For more details, refer to [Cribl Edge Windows Event Logs Source Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/edge/sources-windows-event-logs/).

item_1765683336265.label: Kafka
item_1765683336265.title: Configure Kafka Source in Cribl Stream [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765683336265.content:
- [ ] Navigate to **Data > Sources** in **Cribl Stream**.
- [ ]  Select **Kafka** and click **Add Source**.
- [ ] Fill in the required fields:
- **Input ID**: Provide a unique name for the source.
- **Bootstrap servers**: Enter the **hostname** and **port** of Kafka brokers (e.g., **mykafkabroker:9092**).
- **Topic**: Enter the name(s) of topics to subscribe to. Press **Enter/Return** between multiple entries.
- [ ] Ensure **Group ID** is unique for each Kafka Source to optimize performance and prevent excessive rebalancing.
- [ ] **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**.

For more details, refer to [Kafka Source Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-kafka).

item_1765683882112.label: Office 365 Activity
item_1765683882112.title: Configure Office 365 Activity Source in Cribl Stream [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765683882112.content:
- [ ] Navigate to **Data > Sources** in **Cribl Stream**. 
- [ ] Select **Microsoft > Office 365 Activity** and click **Add Source**. 
- [ ] Fill in the **General Settings** fields:
- **Input ID**: Provide a unique name for the source (e.g., O365_Activity_Logs).
- **Description**: (Optional) Describe the source. ☐ Configure API Authentication:
- **Client ID**: Enter the Application (client) ID of your Azure AD application.
- **Client Secret**: Enter the secret Value generated for your Azure AD application.
- **Tenant ID**: Enter the Directory (tenant) ID of your Office 365 tenant. ☐ Configure API Settings:
- **Content Types**: Specify the log types you want to pull (e.g., Audit.AzureActiveDirectory, Audit.Exchange, Audit.SharePoint).
- **Polling Interval**: Set how frequently (in seconds) Cribl Stream checks for new log subscriptions and content (Default is 300 seconds / 5 minutes).
- **Maximum Concurrent Content Streams**: Set the maximum number of concurrent connections for content polling (Default is 10). 
- [ ] Review **Data Settings** (e.g., enable Pre-process JSON for faster processing). 
- [ ] Click **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**.

For more details, refer to the [Office 365 Activity Source Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-microsoft-365-activity/).

item_1765751808266.label: Splunk TCP
item_1765751808266.title: Configure Splunk TCP Source in Cribl Stream [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765751808266.content:
- [ ] Navigate to **Data > Sources** in **Cribl Stream**.
- [ ] Select **Splunk TCP** and select **Add Source** (or clone and modify the preconfigured **in_splunk_tcp**).
- [ ] Configure the following under General Settings:
- **Input ID**: Enter a unique name (if cloning/adding new).• Address: Enter the hostname/IP to listen on (e.g., 0.0.0.0 or localhost).
- **Port**: Enter the port number (default is **9997**).
- [ ] **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**.

For more details, refer to [Splunk TCP Source Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-splunk/).

item_1765752370674.label: Splunk Forwarder
item_1765752370674.title: Configure Splunk Forwarder to send to Cribl Stream [CUSTOMER]
item_1765752370674.content:
Enable the Splunk TCP Source and use its actual endpoint and TLS configuration in the forwarder output group. Decide explicitly whether traffic is rerouted or cloned; multiple default output groups can duplicate delivery. Use customer-approved index routing rather than example IP addresses. Back up and validate the forwarder configuration with the installed Splunk version. Test receipt in Cribl and the final Splunk index before changing production routing.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-splunk.md

item_1765833587524.label: Splunk HEC
item_1765833587524.title: Configure Splunk HEC Destination in Cribl Stream [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765833587524.content:
- [ ] Navigate to **Data > Destinations** in **Cribl Stream**.
- [ ] Select **Splunk > HEC** and click **Add Destination**.
- [ ] Fill in the required fields:
- **Output ID**: Provide a descriptive name for the destination.
- **Splunk HEC Endpoints**: Enter the endpoint URL (e.g., https://http-inputs-YOURCLOUDORGHERE.splunkcloud.com/services/collector/event).
- **Authentication Method**: Set to Manual.
- **HEC Auth Token**: Enter the Splunk HEC API access token.
- [ ] Click **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**.

For more details, refer to [Splunk HEC Destination Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-splunk-hec).

item_1765859842239.label: Splunk Load Balanced
item_1765859842239.title: Configure Splunk Load Balanced Destination in Cribl Stream [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765859842239.content:
- [ ] Navigate to **Data > Destinations** in **Cribl Stream**. 
- [ ] Select **Splunk > Splunk Load Balanced** and click **Add Destination**. 
- [ ] Fill in the required fields under General Settings: 
- **Output ID**: Provide a descriptive name for the destination. 
- Ensure **Indexer discovery** is toggled **off** (or, if enabled, fill in the **Cluster Manager URI** and **Authentication details**). 
- [ ] Under the **Destinations** section fill in the reciever details.  If more than one, click **Add Destination** and repeat for each additional indexer.
- **Address**: Enter the Splunk Indexer hostname or IP address (e.g., splunkindexer01.local). 
- **Port**: Enter the Splunk receiver port (e.g., **9997**). 
- **Load weight**: Set the relative traffic weight (e.g., 10). 
- [ ] Click **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**.

For more details, refer to [Splunk Load Balanced Destination Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-splunk-lb/).

item_1765891504093.label: Office 365 Message Trace
item_1765891504093.title: Configure Office 365 Message Trace Source in Cribl Stream [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765891504093.content:
- [ ] Navigate to **Data > Sources** in **Cribl Stream**. 
- [ ] Select **Microsoft > Office 365 Message Trace** and click **Add Source**. 
- [ ] Fill in the General Settings fields:
- **Output ID**: Provide a unique name for the source (e.g., O365_Msg_Trace).
- **Description**: (Optional) Describe the source.
- **Report URL**: Retain the default (https://reports.office365.com/ecp/reportingwebservice/reporting.svc/MessageTrace) or enter a custom URL.
- **Poll interval**: Set how often (in minutes) to run the report (Must divide evenly into 60, e.g., 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, or 60).
- [ ] Configure **Authentication** (using the default OAuth method):
- **Client ID**: Enter the Application (client) ID of your Azure AD application.
- **Client secret**: Directly enter the client secret Value generated for your Azure AD application.
- **Tenant identifier**: Enter the Directory (tenant) ID of your Office 365 tenant.
- **Resource**: Retain the default (https://outlook.office365.com).
- [ ] Click **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**.

For more details, refer to the [Office 365 Message Trace Source Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-microsoft365-msg-trace/)

item_1765913670681.label: Sentinel (Prepare Azure Workspace)
item_1765913670681.title: Prepare the Azure Workspace [CUSTOMER]
item_1765913670681.content:
Register the Azure application and retain tenant/client IDs and its supported credential securely. Define the target table schema and matching DCR stream. Prefer DCR kind:direct with its embedded logIngestion endpoint when appropriate; a separate DCE is needed for cases such as Private Link. Assign Monitoring Metrics Publisher on the DCR to the application. Preserve the case and type of TimeGenerated. Validate a record in the target table before sending production data.

Prepare the receiving service before configuring the Cribl Destination. Confirm: Azure table schema / DCR stream declaration / DCR endpoint / application role assignment. Use the authentication, payload and permissions required by the linked guide and current customer subscription. Do not reuse example endpoints or secrets. Configure the Cribl Destination with those values, test connectivity, send a sample event and verify the final record, timestamp and fields in the receiver. Record throughput, retry behavior and any rate limits. Vendor console navigation and licensing must be validated for the installed service.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/usecase-azure-workspace.md

item_1765916059645.label: Azure Microsoft Sentinel
item_1765916059645.title: Configure Azure Microsoft Sentinel Destination [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765916059645.content:
- [ ] Go to **Data > Destinations**.
- [ ] Search for **Azure Microsoft Sentinel**, click the tile.
- [ ] Click **Add Destination** button in the upper right.
- [ ] Fill in the **General Settings** fields:
- **Output ID**: Enter a unique name for the destination.
- **Endpoint configuration**: Select URL.
- **URL**: Paste the ingestion URL obtained by running the query in the Azure Resource Graph Explorer.  Make sure Endpoint configuration is set to **URL**.
- [ ] Select **Authentication** in the left panel.
- **Login URL**: the endpoint for the OAuth API call, which is expected to be a POST call. This URL takes the form **https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/oauth2/v2.0/token**.
- **OAuth secret**: should be set to the **secret value** from your **credentials creation** when you create your app registration.
- [ ] **Client ID** was also captured during the **App registration**.

For more details, refer to [Azure Microsoft Sentinel Destination Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-sentinel/).

item_1765935176719.label: S3 Bucket
item_1765935176719.title: Configure AWS S3 Bucket for Cribl Stream Destination [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765935176719.content:
Grant s3:PutObject to the configured identity for the target object prefix. s3:ListBucket is required unless bucket-existence verification is disabled; s3:GetBucketLocation is required if Region is not configured. Validate the selected encryption permissions and ensure staging storage is sized for outages. Confirm object creation after the flush interval and read the produced object.

Prepare the receiving service before configuring the Cribl Destination. Confirm: S3 bucket / region / prefix / IAM object-writing policy / encryption. Use the authentication, payload and permissions required by the linked guide and current customer subscription. Do not reuse example endpoints or secrets. Configure the Cribl Destination with those values, test connectivity, send a sample event and verify the final record, timestamp and fields in the receiver. Record throughput, retry behavior and any rate limits. Vendor console navigation and licensing must be validated for the installed service.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-s3.md

item_1766077477603.label: Use Case: Search cached results
item_1766077477603.title: Use Case: Searching cached results of previous job
item_1766077477603.content:
Run a bounded initial search and copy its job ID from History. To reuse available results, query: `dataset="$vt_results" jobId="YOUR_JOB_ID_HERE"`. Apply the intended analysis to that result set, then restore the original dataset query when validating the complete data. Reusing results does not rerun the original query, but still consumes search credits; opening the cached History result is different. Access depends on permissions and history TTL. Do not treat the cached subset as the full dataset.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/search/vt_results.md

item_1766117579461.label: Vendor Side: S3 Bucket
item_1766117579461.title: Configure S3 Bucket to allow Cribl Search to search the bucket [CUSTOMER]
item_1766117579461.content:
Configure Search access independently of Stream Source/Destination permissions. Check: S3: AWS role trust and permission policies generated for the Search provider; bucket paths, region and supported datatypes. Create the provider and federated dataset in the intended Search context; do not confuse an external provider with an ingested Search dataset. Set path filters, datatype and event-time/partition-time handling explicitly. Test a known object, a bounded time range and query permissions. Review the complete linked guide for current authentication methods, format support and limitations.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/search/set-up-s3.md
https://docs.cribl.io/search/basic-concepts.md

item_1767819338153.label: Splunk HEC
item_1767819338153.title: Configure Splunk HEC in Splunk [CUSTOMER]
item_1767819338153.content:
Create a HEC token enabled for the intended index and copy the actual HEC endpoint. Follow the Destination guide for the chosen event/raw endpoint. Do not enable Indexer Acknowledgement on the Splunk token for this documented integration; it can cause missing-channel errors. Validate TLS and confirm index, sourcetype and event time in Splunk.

Prepare the receiving service before configuring the Cribl Destination. Confirm: Splunk HEC token / enabled index / HEC endpoint / acknowledgement support. Use the authentication, payload and permissions required by the linked guide and current customer subscription. Do not reuse example endpoints or secrets. Configure the Cribl Destination with those values, test connectivity, send a sample event and verify the final record, timestamp and fields in the receiver. Record throughput, retry behavior and any rate limits. Vendor console navigation and licensing must be validated for the installed service.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-splunk-hec.md

item_1768941518552.title: Configure Cribl Lake Dataset [CUSTOMER & CRIBL]
item_1768941518552.content:
Create the Lake Dataset in the intended Storage Location. Set retention according to the contract and storage-location constraints; Azure locations with default retention inherit that value. Choose JSON for storage efficiency or Parquet for appropriate structured data. Lake Datasets support up to three Lake Partitions; do not conflate these with Search engine indexing settings. Verify the compatible federated Dataset Type and datatype in Search. Test ingestion, search and replay. Shortening retention can remove existing data; review before saving.

Official configuration and limitations:

item_1769139466529.label: Sumo Logic
item_1769139466529.title: Configure Sumo Logic Destination in Cribl Stream [CUSTOMER & CRIBL]
item_1769139466529.content:
- [ ] Navigate to **Data > Destinations** in Cribl Stream. 
- [ ] Select **Sumo Logic** and click **Add Destination**. 
- [ ] Fill in the **General Settings**: 
- **Output ID**: Provide a unique, descriptive name (e.g., sumo_logic_prod). 
- **API URL**: Paste the **Sumo Logic HTTP Source endpoint URL** (e.g., https://endpoint.sumologic.com/receiver/v1/http/...). 
- [ ] (Optional) Configure **Sumo Logic Specifics**: 
- **Custom source name**: Override the default source name (or use the __sourceName field). 
- **Custom source category**: Override the default source category (or use the __sourceCategory field). 
- [ ] Configure **Optional Settings**: 
- **Data Format**: Set to JSON (default) or Raw to preserve the original format. 
- **Compression**: Select Gzip to reduce data payload size (recommended by Sumo Logic). 
- [ ] (Optional) Configure **Advanced Settings**: 
- **Safe headers**: Declare any non-sensitive headers to log in plaintext. 
- **Persistent Queue**: Set the Mode (e.g., Smart or Always On) to handle backpressure or network outages. 
- [ ] Click **Save**. 
- [ ] Click **Commit & Deploy**.

For more details, refer to [Sumo Logic Destination Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-sumo-logic/).

item_1769182409963.label: Test Sumo (delete me)
item_1769182409963.title: Testing AI Output
item_1769182409963.content:

- [ ] Navigate to **Data > Destinations** in **Cribl Stream**.

item_1769197445356.content:

item_1770408232396.content:
***Prerequisites***
- [ ] Ensure **Git** is installed on the Cribl Stream Leader node to enable configuration version control and commits.
- [ ] Obtain the **Event Hub Connection String** from the Azure Portal.
  - The connection string requires **Listen** permissions.
- [ ] Identify the target **Event Hub Name** and **Consumer Group**.
- [ ] (Optional) Provision a **Redis** instance if external checkpointing is required for high availability across Worker Nodes.

***Configure Azure Event Hubs Source***
- [ ] Navigate to **Stream > Data > Sources**.
- [ ] Search for and select **Azure Event Hubs**.
- [ ] Click **Add Source** to create a new configuration.

***General Settings***
- [ ] **Input ID**: Enter a unique name for this source definition (e.g., `az_eventhub_logs`).
- [ ] **Event Hub Name**: Enter the name of the specific Event Hub within the Namespace.
- [ ] **Consumer Group**: Enter the Azure Consumer Group name.
  - Default: `$Default`.

***Authentication***
- [ ] Select the desired **Authentication** method:
  - **Connection String**:
    - [ ] Select **Enter Connection String**.
    - [ ] Paste the full connection string (starts with `Endpoint=sb://...`).
  - **Manual Entry**:
    - [ ] Select **Manual Entry**.
    - [ ] **Namespace FQDN**: Enter the fully qualified domain name (e.g., `namespace.servicebus.windows.net`).
    - [ ] **Shared Access Key Name**: Enter the SAS Key Name.
    - [ ] **Shared Access Key**: Enter the SAS Key value.
  - **Managed Identity**:
    - [ ] Toggle **Use Managed Identity** to **Yes**.
    - [ ] Ensure the Azure VM hosting the Worker has the **Azure Event Hubs Data Receiver** role.

***Advanced Settings***
- [ ] **Checkpointing**: Select the persistence method for read offsets.
  - **Memory**: Offsets are stored in memory and lost on restart.
  - **Disk**: Offsets are stored on the local filesystem.
  - **Redis**: Offsets are stored in an external Redis instance (Recommended for distributed Worker Groups).
- [ ] If **Redis** is selected:
  - [ ] **Redis URL**: Enter the address of the Redis server (e.g., `redis://10.0.0.5:6379`).
- [ ] **Socket Timeout (ms)**: Define the inactivity duration before closing the connection (Default: `60000`).

***Finalizing Configuration***
- [ ] Click **Save**.
- [ ] Click **Commit & Deploy** at the top right to push the configuration to Worker Nodes.
- [ ] Verify data flow on the **Live Data** tab.

item_1770408232396.title: Configure Azure Event Hubs Source in Cribl [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]

item_1770408493491.content:
***Prerequisites***
- [ ] Ensure you have access to a Worker Group in Cribl Stream.
- [ ] Confirm the target Azure Blob Storage Container and associated Azure Queue (or Service Bus) are configured in the Azure Portal.
- [ ] Obtain the necessary Azure connection details (Connection Strings, Account Keys, or SAS Tokens) if not using Managed Identity.

***Navigation***
- [ ] Log in to Cribl Stream.
- [ ] Select the desired **Worker Group**.
- [ ] Navigate to **Data > Sources**.
- [ ] Select **Azure > Azure Blob** from the list or use the search bar.
- [ ] Click **Add Source**.

***General Settings***
- [ ] **Input ID**: Enter a unique name for this source (e.g., `azure_blob_app_logs`).
- [ ] **Queue Type**: Select the notification queue mechanism:
  - **Azure Queue Storage**: Standard storage queue.
  - **Service Bus**: Azure Service Bus queue or topic.
- [ ] **Authentication Method**: Choose the authentication strategy:
  - **Auto**: Uses the Worker Node's Managed Identity (requires Azure environment).
  - **Manual**: Requires **Account Name** and **Account Key**.
  - **Connection String**: Requires the full Azure Connection String.
  - **Text Secret**: References a secret stored in the KMS.
- [ ] **Queue Name**: Enter the specific name of the Azure Queue or Service Bus Queue/Topic to poll for event notifications.
- [ ] **Container Name**: Enter the name of the Azure Blob Storage container where the actual data files reside.
- [ ] **Blob Path Filter**: (Optional) Define a glob pattern to limit ingestion to specific files (e.g., `logs/app/*.json`).

***Processing Settings***
- [ ] **Pipeline**: Choose the Pipeline to process the incoming data (default: `main`).
- [ ] **Pre-Processing Pipeline**: (Optional) Select a pipeline for data normalization before the main pipeline.

***Advanced Settings***
- [ ] **Parquet**: Toggle on if the source blobs are in Parquet format.
- [ ] **Event Breakers**: Select a specific ruleset if **Auto** does not correctly parse event boundaries.
- [ ] **Max Messages**: (Optional) Set the maximum number of messages to retrieve per poll cycle.
- [ ] **Visibility Timeout**: (Optional) Define how long (in seconds) a message remains invisible to other consumers after retrieval.

***Finalization***
- [ ] Click **Save**.
- [ ] Click **Commit & Deploy** at the top right to push the configuration to your Worker Nodes.

item_1771618263930.label: XSIAM
item_1771618263930.title: Configure Palo XSIAM Destination in Cribl [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1771618263930.content:
***Cortex XSIAM Destination Configuration Checklist***

- [ ] **Prepare XSIAM Environment**
  - Obtain the XSIAM endpoint URL (Format: `https://api-{tenant external URL}/logs/v1/event`).
  - Generate a **Bearer Token** within the Palo Alto XSIAM console for authentication.
- [ ] **Install Palo Alto XSIAM Pack**
  - Navigate to **Processing > Packs** from the Worker Group submenu.
  - Add the **Palo Alto XSIAM Pack** to extract and map mandatory fields required by XSIAM.
- [ ] **Create XSIAM Destination**
  - Navigate to **Data > Destinations** (Stream) or **More > Destinations** (Edge).
  - Select **Cortex XSIAM** from the tiles and click **Add Destination**.
- [ ] **Configure General Settings**
  - **Output ID**: Enter a unique name for the destination.
  - **XSIAM endpoint**: Paste the XSIAM API URL obtained in the first step.
- [ ] **Configure Authentication**
  - Select an **Authentication method** (Bearer Token or Secret).
  - Enter the **Auth token** or select a stored secret.
- [ ] **Tune Advanced Settings (Optional)**
  - **Flush period**: Set to `1` second or greater to control batch latency.
  - **Throttle request rate limit**: Adjust if you need to stay below the default `400` requests per second.
- [ ] **Configure Post-Processing**
  - Attach the **Palo Alto XSIAM Pack** as a **Post-Processing Pipeline** to ensure data is correctly formatted before delivery.
- [ ] **Set Backpressure Behavior**
  - Navigate to **Advanced Settings > Backpressure Behavior**.
  - Choose between **Block**, **Drop new data**, or enable **Persistent Queueing** (PQ) to prevent data loss.
- [ ] **Test and Save**
  - Use the **Test** tab to validate connectivity to the XSIAM endpoint.
  - Click **Save** and **Commit/Deploy** the changes to the Worker Group.

***XSIAM Data Limits Reference***
TABLE: Limit Type,Value
Individual Event Limit,5 MB
Batch Size Limit,9.5 MB
Default Rate Limit,400 requests/sec
Content-Type,`application/json`

item_1773685963528.label: Amazon S3
item_1773685963528.title: Configure Amazon S3 Destination in Stream
item_1773685963528.content:
***Amazon S3 Destination Configuration Checklist***

- [ ] ***Navigation and Initial Setup***
  - Navigate to **Data > Destinations** (or **Routing > QuickConnect**)
  - Select **Amazon S3** from the tiles
  - Click **Add Destination**

- [ ] ***General Settings***
  - Enter a unique **Output ID**
  - Provide the **S3 bucket name**
    - *Note: This can be a constant or a JS expression evaluated at init time*
  - Define the **Staging location** - *Used to locally buffer files before upload; must be high-performance*
  - Set the **Key prefix** - *The root directory prepended to paths (use JS expression for dynamic paths)*
  - Select the **Data format**
    - `JSON` (Default, recommended for Replay)
    - `Raw` (Writes the `_raw` field content)
    - `Parquet` (Requires additional configuration in the **Parquet Settings** tab)

- [ ] ***Authentication***
  - Choose an **Authentication method**:
    - `Auto` (Uses IAM Roles if running on AWS)
    - `Manual` (Requires **Access key** and **Secret key**)
    - `Secret` (References a stored Cribl Secret)
  - If using cross-account access, toggle **Enable for S3** (Assume Role) to **Yes**
    - Enter the **AssumeRole ARN**
    - Enter the **External ID** (if required by the destination account)

- [ ] ***Optional & Advanced Tuning***
  - Select the correct **Region** for the bucket
  - Define a **Partitioning expression** - *Defines how files are organized on S3 (e.g., date-based or by metadata)*
  - Set **Backpressure behavior** to `Block` or `Drop`
  - Adjust **Limit Settings** (under Advanced):
    - **Max file size (MB)**: Max uncompressed size before closing
    - **Max file open time (sec)**: Max duration to keep a file open
    - **Max open files**: Concurrent file limit per Worker process

- [ ] ***Validation and Deployment***
  - Click **Save**
  - **Commit** and **Deploy** the changes to the Worker Group
  - Navigate to **Monitoring > Destinations** to verify the green checkmark status

item_1776968036485.label: Azure Event Hubs
item_1776968036485.title: Configure Azure Event Hubs to Send to Cribl Stream
item_1776968036485.content:
Provision an Event Hub namespace/tier that supports the Kafka endpoint used by this Source. Configure diagnostic settings for the intended Azure resources and a dedicated consumer group. Allow TLS connectivity to the Kafka endpoint on 9093. Prefer a dedicated service principal with the minimum documented RBAC permissions; if using SAS, scope it to the required reading access rather than defaulting to RootManageSharedAccessKey. Configure the supported authentication method and validate a test event plus consumer lag.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-azure-event-hubs.md

item_1777299264060.label: Direct Access - Splunk Cloud Self Storage (DDSS)
item_1777299264060.title: Configuring Direct Access in Lake for Splunk Cloud Self Storage (DDSS)
item_1777299264060.content:
Obtain the Splunk Cloud ID and configure the Splunk Cloud Direct Access Source in Lake. Exchange the bucket name and policy with the Splunk Self Storage configuration, provision the integration and test the connection before creating the dataset. One Splunk Cloud Direct Access Source is supported per Workspace. The dataset uses the default Cribl Lake Storage Location and is read-only to Stream/Search. Validate region alignment and the DDSS/Splunk Journal datatype. Deleting the Lake Source deletes the archived data; deleting the linked Splunk Self Storage location stops new archival without deleting data already in Lake.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/lake/splunk-cloud.md
https://docs.cribl.io/lake/direct-access.md

item_1777403480456.label: S3 / SQS Config
item_1777403480456.title: Configuring S3 / SQS for Ingestion via Cribl S3 Pull Source [CUSTOMER]
item_1777403480456.content:
Configure S3 object-created notifications to the SQS queue. The queue resource policy grants sqs:SendMessage to the S3 service, scoped to the source bucket/account. Cribl requires s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket plus sqs:ReceiveMessage, sqs:DeleteMessage, sqs:ChangeMessageVisibility, sqs:GetQueueAttributes and sqs:GetQueueUrl. With object tagging, add s3:GetObjectTagging and s3:PutObjectTagging. For encrypted data, authorize kms:Decrypt in IAM and the key policy as applicable. Validate regional compatibility, prefix filters and delivery of a newly created object.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-s3.md

item_1777404476756.label: Zscaler NSS
item_1777404476756.title: Configure Zscaler NSS to Send to Cribl.Cloud (Splunk HEC) [CUSTOMER]
item_1777404476756.content:
Confirm whether the customer uses appliance NSS or Cloud NSS; they are different forwarding configurations. Configure the matching Cribl Source and copy its actual HTTPS endpoint, path and authentication settings into the supported Zscaler feed. Use the current Zscaler feed format rather than a generic HEC template. Validate TLS, an example event and sustained delivery. Vendor feed licensing, menus and deployment prerequisites must be confirmed in the current Zscaler documentation.

Official configuration and limitations:
https://docs.cribl.io/stream/sources-zscaler-hec.md

item_1777404544665.label: Zscaler Cloud NSS
item_1777404544665.title: Configure Zscaler Cloud NSS Source in Cribl [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1777404544665.content:
***Cribl Stream Configuration***

- [ ] Enable the **Zscaler HEC Source**
  - Navigate to **Data > Sources** and select **Push > Zscaler Cloud NSS**.
  - Click **Add Source**.
- [ ] Configure **General Settings**
  - **Input ID**: Enter a unique name (e.g., `zscaler_nss`).
  - **Port**: 8088 (disable Splunk HEC source to free up this port)
- [ ] Configure **Security/TLS**
  - Set **TLS** to `Enabled` (Required for Zscaler Cloud connectivity).
  - Provide a **Certificate path** ($CRIBL_CLOUD_CRT) and **Private key path** ($CRIBL_CLOUD_KEY) if using a custom domain.
- [ ] **Save and Deploy**
  - Click **Save**, then **Commit** and **Deploy** the changes to your Worker Group.
- [ ] Determine your **Cribl Endpoint URL**
  - For Cribl Cloud, this is typically `https://in.<organization_id>.cribl.cloud:8088/v1/receiver`.

item_1780671533356.label: Datadog
item_1780671533356.title: Obtain API Key and Determine Region from Datadog
item_1780671533356.content:
Prepare the receiving service before configuring the Cribl Destination. Confirm: Datadog site / API key / logs or metrics endpoint. Use the authentication, payload and permissions required by the linked guide and current customer subscription. Do not reuse example endpoints or secrets. Configure the Cribl Destination with those values, test connectivity, send a sample event and verify the final record, timestamp and fields in the receiver. Record throughput, retry behavior and any rate limits. Vendor console navigation and licensing must be validated for the installed service.

Official configuration and limitations:

item_1780671814476.label: Datadog
item_1780671814476.title: Configuring Datadog Destination in Cribl Stream [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1780671814476.content:
- [ ] In **Cribl Stream**, navigate to **Data > Destinations**.
- [ ] Select **Datadog** and click **Add Destination**.
- [ ] Fill in the required fields:
- **Output ID**: Provide a unique name for the destination.
- **Authentication Method**:** select Manual to enter an API key.
- **API Key**: Enter your Datadog organization's API key.
- **Datadog site**: Select the Datadog region your are sending to.  Defaults to US.
- **Send logs as**: specify how event payloads are delivered:
  - `application/json` (Default: structured JSON objects)
  - `text/plain` (Newline `\n` delimited raw strings)
- **Message field**: with the exact field name hosting your core payload. Leaving it blank defaults to sending the entire JSON object.  Set to **_raw**.
- **Datadog tags**: List of tags to send with logs. (e.g., `env:prod,app:billing`).
- [ ] Click **Save** then **Commit and Deploy**.

item_1781127766513.label: CrowdStrike FDR
item_1781127766513.title: Configuring the CrowdStrike FDR Source in Stream [CUSTOMER & CRIBL]
item_1781127766513.content:
***Prerequisites (Obtain from CrowdStrike Admin)***
- [ ] Secure the **FDR Credentials** and parameters needed for data retrieval:
  - AWS Access Key
  - AWS Secret Key
  - SQS Queue URL (or Name/ARN)
  - AWS Region (where the S3 bucket and SQS queue reside)

***Configure the CrowdStrike FDR Source in Cribl Stream***
- [ ] Navigate to **Data > Sources** in **Cribl Stream**.
- [ ] Select **CrowdStrike FDR** and click **Add Source**.
- [ ] Fill in the ***General Settings*** fields:
  - **Input ID**: Provide a unique name for the source (e.g., CrowdStrike_FDR_logs).
  - **Queue**: The name, URL, or ARN of the SQS queue to read notifications from. (e.g., 'https://host:port/myQueueName').
- [ ] Configure the ***Optional Settings*** panel:
  - Set the appropriate **Region** matching the bucket and queue location if it is not explicitly built into the Queue URL.
- [ ] Configure the ***Authentication*** panel:
  - Select **Manual** authentication.
  - Paste your CrowdStrike-provided AWS **Access key** and **Secret key** into their respective text boxes.
